rationale: Iteration 0 has no race telemetry yet, so this is a conservative baseline meant to finish the course and produce measurements. Speed: the run must cover about 4-5 m in under 3 s (about 1.5 m/s average), so base_speed is set to 1.4, high enough to be near the required pace but below full voltage to limit wheel slip and overshoot on bends. Sensing: five sensors spread across the body at x = +0.04, +0.02, 0, -0.02, -0.04, placed 0.05 m ahead of the axle so they read the line before the wheels reach it. Sensor size 0.012 m (half the 25 mm tape width gives good coverage at this spacing). Weights are linear in x (1, 0.5, 0, -0.5, -1), so signal equals the lateral tape offset in roughly sensor-spacing units and positive steers left as required. Control: kp = 3.0 gives about 1050 PWM of wheel differential per unit of signal, enough to correct a 2 cm offset without saturating. kd = 0.1 adds mild damping against oscillation; ki = 0 avoids integral windup on bends. Line loss uses last_direction so the robot turns back toward the side it last saw the line. Geometry: wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body_width 0.12 m (a wider off-track limit gives more tolerance), body_length 0.16 m, mass 0.8 kg. Hypotheses to test: (1) the robot completes the course with few line-loss events at this speed; (2) if steering_oscillation is high, kp is too large relative to kd; (3) if completion_time exceeds 3 s, base_speed must rise. Next measurements needed: completion, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation. Expected result: completion with moderate rms_error, with the speed/oscillation trade-off showing where to tune next.
